_README: CLAIMS THAT MONEY WAS MISSING, AND WHAT SOMEBODY DID ABOUT IT.
"The processor has not seen this money" is a reading of one moment. It is
not a fact about the deal, and it expires. A payment can land the next day;
a row with no prospect email reads as unmatched however much the buyer paid.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-24]: "what tends to
happen is u tell me theres no 750$ collected in the whop and then i tell u to
0 it out, but then the payment comes in or u just didnt look properly and u
never end up updating." That is the whole failure. Somebody edits a figure on
the strength of a check, the check turns out to have been early or wrong, and
the corrected figure sits there being wrong for ever because nothing ever
asks the question a second time.
So every time a missing-money finding is ACTED ON - a figure changed, a row
corrected, a call excluded - it gets written down here. `npm run check:claims`
re-asks the processor about every open claim on every run, and shouts when
money has since arrived. A claim is never closed by time passing; it is closed
by a person, with a reason.
It has already caught two: Liam's $750, which arrived on the day of the call
and was about to be deleted from the tracker, and Jonathan Laguna's $4,000,
which had been in Whop for a day when his call was excluded for not being in
Whop.
STATUS is one of: open (still believed), reopened (money has since been
found - somebody must undo what they did), closed (ruled on by a person, with
a reason and a date).

claims.claim: No payment of $750 was found in Whop for this call.
claims.acted_on: The team was told to change Collected On Call to $0 on the tracker row.
claims.resolution: 2026-08-24: Whop shows liamb2507@yahoo.com paid $750 on 2026-08-20, the day of the call. The instruction was retracted before anybody carried it out. [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-24: 'yes then mark the 750$'] The row stands at $750.
claims.closed_because: Moayad ruled the $750 stands. The instruction to zero it was retracted before anybody carried it out, so nothing needs undoing.

claims.claim: This $4,000 never entered Brey's Whop account, so the call belongs to another offer.
claims.acted_on: The call was excluded from both dashboards.
claims.resolution: 2026-08-24: Whop shows jonathanlagunas147@gmail.com paid $2,500 and $1,500 on 2026-08-21, on Brey's only product. The row simply carries no prospect email, which is what made it read as unmatched. The exclusion was reversed and the call is back on both dashboards.
claims.closed_because: The exclusion was reversed the same day and the call is back on both dashboards, so nothing is left wrong.

claims.claim: Collected On Call was $3,250 and Whop has never seen a cent from Alan Campos. Checked under a.campos@rocketmail.com, chrispindec@gmail.com and any name containing Campos.
claims.acted_on: Collected On Call zeroed. The $5,000 deal value is UNTOUCHED — the recording owns what was agreed and he did agree to $5,000, so the deal stands with $5,000 outstanding. His Prospect Email was also corrected from chrispindec@gmail.com to a.campos@rocketmail.com: the invite carried TWO external attendees and the workflow took the first, so any payment he makes would not have matched his call.
claims.why_this_one_is_easy_to_get_wrong: Fathom's summary says 'Paid a $3,250 deposit via Clarity Pay', which reads as money received. Two lines later the same summary says a plan was DECLINED for want of ~$341 and that Alan still has to move ~$1,500 out of E*Trade. And ClarityPay money does reach Whop: on 2026-08-23 a $3,000 ClarityPay deal landed as $700 plus $2,300. So the processor's silence is not a missing integration, it is an answer.
claims.reopen_if: Any payment appears in Whop for Alan Campos. It may yet — his own plan was to transfer the funds. If it lands, put Collected On Call back.
